question:
Thirteen shaded and six unshaded hexagonal tiles were used to create the figure below. If a new figure is created by attaching a border of unshaded tiles with the same size and shape as the others, what will be the difference between the total number of unshaded tiles and the total number of shaded tiles in the new figure?

[Figure 1](figures/2004_AMC_8_Q15_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Count the added tiles in separate horizontal rows. The original figure has five rows containing \(3,4,5,4,3\) tiles. Adding a border extends each of these five rows by one tile at each end. It also creates a new row of four tiles above the figure and another row of four below it.

These groups cover the entire border without overlap: the top and bottom rows are new, and the other added tiles occupy the two ends of the five original rows. Thus the border contains
\[
4+4+5\cdot2=18
\]
tiles. All of them are unshaded, so the new figure has \(6+18=24\) unshaded tiles and still has \(13\) shaded tiles. The difference is
\[
24-13=\boxed{11},
\]
choice \(\text{C}\).
